regulator: Ministry of Health, through the Analytical Expertise Center (Analitik Ekspertiza Mərkəzi) – https://sehiyye.gov.az

facts.title: Regulator and legal basis
facts.body: Medicines are registered by the Ministry of Health acting through the Analytical Expertise Center, under the Law on Medicines and the Rules of State Registration approved by Cabinet of Ministers Resolution 345 of 18 July 2024 (in force from 20 July 2024, replacing the 2007 rules). Only registered medicines may be imported, produced, sold or used; the state register is published as open data (about 11,300 entries).

facts.title: Primary review in 15 working days, expertise in 90 calendar days
facts.body: The 2023 amendments to the Law on Medicines set a primary examination of 15 working days and a specialised examination of 90 calendar days for new registrations and re-registrations. The Ministry issues the certificate within seven business days of a positive expert report. Deficiencies are notified within five business days and corrected within ten; the clock pauses meanwhile.

facts.title: Simplified recognition for reference-country approvals
facts.body: Medicines registered by the authorities of a list of reference countries (stringent regulators) are registered through a recognition procedure of nine working days including the examination, on the strength of the foreign assessment.

facts.title: Instructions in Azerbaijani, notarised
facts.body: The patient information and summary of product characteristics are translated into Azerbaijani and the translation notarised; the Center checks it and the Ministry approves it. Approved instructions for every registered medicine are published as PDFs on the Center's site.

facts.title: Five-year certificate, re-registration 90 days before expiry
facts.body: Each product gets its own certificate, valid five years; re-registration is filed at least 90 days before expiry and the new certificate takes effect the day after the old one ends. Registration can be cancelled for poor pharmacovigilance, a negative benefit-risk assessment, GMP failures or quality failures in three batches.

facts.title: State-regulated prices through the Tariff Council
facts.body: Registered medicines are on the list of goods with state-regulated prices: the Tariff Council sets the maximum wholesale and retail prices of each registered medicine, and medicines may only be sold at or below them. Budget for price registration after marketing authorisation.

facts.title: Examination fees
facts.body: The Center charges examination fees per product; service providers quote about AZN 1,000 to 1,300 including VAT per product for the full examination (around USD 600 to 800). Ask the Center for the current schedule before budgeting.

facts.title: Import permits and taxes
facts.body: Imports of registered medicines need an import permit from the Center. The standard VAT is 18% and the customs tariff on medicines is in the low band; exemptions apply to specific lists set by the Cabinet of Ministers. Check the current treatment of your tariff line with a broker.

routes.label: Full review (national)
routes.description: Dossier to the Analytical Expertise Center with notarised Azerbaijani instructions: 15 working days of primary review and 90 calendar days of expertise, then the certificate within seven business days. Five-year registration, then price registration with the Tariff Council.

routes.label: Recognition of a reference-country approval
routes.description: For medicines approved by a listed reference authority: registration in nine working days including the examination, on the foreign assessment.
